title: Suppression Threshold Lab
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Student Privacy
Statistical Disclosure Control
Small-Cell Suppression
Learning Analytics Dashboards
Data Ethics
description: A p5.js lab in which learners predict which counts in a small mastery-band table must be hidden under a suppression threshold, see a single hidden cell leak through the row total by subtraction, and apply complementary suppression to close the leak.
audience: Teachers, instructional designers, learning-technology developers and learning-analytics practitioners (college undergraduate and professional development)

educational.topic: Applying a suppression threshold and complementary suppression to a table with row totals
learningObjectives: The learner will apply a suppression threshold and complementary suppression to a small table and predict which cells must be hidden so that no hidden count can be recovered by subtraction.
prerequisites: Identification by elimination in small groups

accessibility.notes: Hidden cells carry a lock and a text tag (below threshold or complement) as well as a color; controls are native and labeled; predictions use native buttons

controls.label: Threshold
controls.purpose: Minimum group size for a published count

controls.label: Apply complementary suppression
controls.purpose: Hide a second cell when a row has exactly one hidden cell

controls.label: Show the subtraction
controls.purpose: Draw the arithmetic that recovers a hidden cell or gives only a sum

controls.label: Reset
controls.purpose: Hide the answers again for a new round of predictions

controls.label: Reveal all
controls.purpose: Show every cell's status at once

controls.label: Hidden
controls.purpose: Predict that the selected cell is hidden

controls.label: Shown
controls.purpose: Predict that the selected cell is shown

controls.label: Table cells
controls.purpose: Select a cell to predict, or read the reason for a revealed cell

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict-then-reveal practice of a rule, followed by exploring the rule's parameters
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Click a cell, predict hidden or shown, get a reasoned answer; then vary threshold and settings
keyQuestions: Which cells fall below the threshold?
Can the row total recover a hidden cell?
Which second cell closes the leak, and why not a zero?
commonMisconceptions: Blanking the small cell is enough when the total is published
Any second cell makes a good complement
Two small cells in a row still need a complement
assessmentOpportunities: Explaining the subtraction that recovers a hidden cell
Justifying the choice of complementary cell

equations: complement = smallest non-zero visible count when exactly one cell in the row is hidden
recovered = row total - sum of visible cells (exact only when one cell is hidden)
assumptions: Zero counts stay visible, as in the chapter's worked example
limitations: Real disclosure control also considers column totals, linked tables and differencing across releases
The design's suppression filter is designed, not built
